## Summary

I evaluated the split fraction (multiples of 0.01, 0.00–0.90) by committing revisions from v17-t06-r1 and solving each with the default policy (120 s wall-time budget). Using 8 solves total (well under the 12-solve limit), I found:

| split | S4 A mole fraction | A recovery |
|---|---|---|
| 0.00 | 0.4625 | 0.8161 |
| 0.50 | 0.4854 | 0.7706 |
| 0.65 | 0.4982 | 0.7432 |
| 0.66 | 0.4992 | 0.7410 |
| **0.67** | **0.50019** | **0.73872** |
| 0.68 | 0.5012 | 0.7364 |
| 0.70 | 0.5034 | 0.7316 |
| 0.90 | 0.5293 | 0.6697 |

Vapor-A purity increases monotonically with split fraction while A recovery decreases monotonically. The 50 mol % A constraint first becomes satisfied at **split_fraction = 0.67** (revision rev-000006), which therefore maximizes A recovery subject to the purity constraint. That solve (job-000006) converged and was VERIFIED.

At split = 0.67: S4.n.A = 0.7387216 mol/s, S4.N = 1.476876 mol/s → A mole fraction = 0.5001919, A recovery = 0.7387216 (73.87%).
